Child Abuse Reporting Procedures

REPORTING FLOWCHART:

SUSPECTED ABUSE/NEGLECT OBSERVED OR DISCLOSED

↓

DO NOT INVESTIGATE - REMAIN OBJECTIVE

↓

DOCUMENT FACTS - WHAT WAS SEEN/HEARD?

↓

IMMEDIATELY REPORT TO DESIGNATED SCHOOL OFFICIAL

(Child Protection Officer/Principal)

↓

SCHOOL OFFICIAL ASSISTS WITH REPORT (IF NEEDED)

↓

MAKE REPORT TO CHILD PROTECTIVE SERVICES

Phone: ______________

↓

FOLLOW-UP WITH WRITTEN REPORT (if required)

↓

COOPERATE WITH INVESTIGATION

↓

MAINTAIN CONFIDENTIALITY

REPORTING CHECKLIST:

☐ Do not confront alleged perpetrator

☐ Do not promise child confidentiality

☐ Listen, do not interrogate

☐ Document exactly what child said (use quotes)

☐ Document observations objectively

☐ Report immediately - do not delay

☐ Include all relevant information:

☐ Child's name, age, address

☐ Parent/guardian information

☐ Nature and extent of suspected abuse/neglect

☐ Basis for suspicion (what was seen/heard)

☐ Child's current location and safety status

☐ Alleged perpetrator information (if known)

☐ Reporter's name and contact information

FOLLOWING A REPORT:

☐ CPS case number received: ______________

☐ Administrator notified of report

☐ Confidentiality maintained (need-to-know basis only)

☐ Support provided to child at school

☐ Documentation stored securely

☐ No retaliation against reporter

Staff Boundaries & Code Of Conduct

STAFF CODE OF CONDUCT - KEY PROVISIONS:

APPROPRIATE INTERACTIONS:

☐ Maintain professional boundaries at all times

☐ Use positive, respectful language with students

☐ Physical contact should be:

☐ Appropriate to the situation

☐ In public view

☐ Brief and non-intimate

☐ With student's consent

☐ Age-appropriate

☐ One-on-one meetings with students should:

☐ Be in visible areas

☐ Have door open/window visible

☐ Be with knowledge of other staff

☐ Avoid isolated locations

PROHIBITED CONDUCT:

☐ No physical discipline of any kind

☐ No romantic or sexual relationships with students

☐ No dating students

☐ No sexually suggestive comments or jokes

☐ No inappropriate touching (hugging beyond brief greeting)

☐ No private communication with students (texts, DMs, social media)

☐ No giving gifts to individual students

☐ No transporting students alone

☐ No meeting students outside of school without parent consent

☐ No favoritism or special treatment

☐ No discussing personal problems with students

☐ No sharing personal contact information

☐ No alcohol/drugs with students

ELECTRONIC COMMUNICATION:

☐ Use school-provided platforms for communication

☐ No personal social media connections with students

☐ All communication should be professional and transparent

☐ Copy parents on electronic communication (for younger students)

☐ No private messaging apps

☐ Save all electronic communication

Student Safety Curriculum & Prevention Education

AGE-APPROPRIATE SAFETY CURRICULUM:

GRADE LEVEL | TOPICS COVERED

PreK-K | Good touch/bad touch, trusted adults, body safety, saying "no"

Grades 1-2 | Personal boundaries, private body parts, secrets vs. surprises, reporting

Grades 3-5 | Bullying prevention, peer pressure, safe/unsafe secrets, online safety

Grades 6-8 | Healthy relationships, consent, digital citizenship, sexting risks, harassment

Grades 9-12 | Dating violence, sexual harassment, consent, bystander intervention, reporting
